challenge.name: The Consent Gap
challenge.description: A new model version requires loyalty basket data, but the deployment pipeline lacks the governance controls to verify consent. #automation_alex# wants to push the automated deployment forward immediately to meet the promotion deadline, while #requirements_reuben# insists on a manual review process to ensure legal compliance. #automation_alex# is open to adding a manual approval step if it keeps the pipeline moving, but #requirements_reuben# will not accept any automated path without full audit trails.

output.content: The new loyalty model version will raise our monthly infrastructure spend. I am willing to accept that higher cost if it cuts residual stock on the middle aisle promotions and improves margin. I give up strict cost control for now to gain better forecast accuracy. This relaxation is not permanent. I will monitor the spend closely and expect the business value to justify the extra expense within two promotion cycles. If the numbers do not improve, we revert to the old budget limit. This trade lets us test the feature set quickly while keeping the finance team comfortable that we are not bleeding capital on unproven infrastructure.
output.reclassify_reason: The author explicitly states they are giving up strict cost control to gain better forecast accuracy, which fits the definition of a trade-off.
